items.finding: The constructor-dispatch and self-use contract are distinct hazards; tests should not conflate field initialization with field visibility.
challenge_requirements: Test virtual dispatch during parent construction

items.finding: Interfaces may be combined with an existing class hierarchy; default/Object method restrictions need explicit compile tests.
challenge_requirements: Compile two capabilities alongside a superclass

items.finding: Locking each primitive call is weaker than synchronizing a compound default method. Compatibility must be analyzed per legacy wrapper rather than assuming all JDK wrappers fail.
challenge_requirements: Do not claim compound atomicity without whole-call lock

items.finding: Constant interfaces leak an implementation choice; a currency threshold may be runtime configuration, not an enum constant.
challenge_requirements: Distinguish typed static identity from mutable business policy

items.finding: A sealed interface controls permitted implementation types, not valid field values. Records are shallowly immutable; explicit validation and defensive ownership are separate requirements.
challenge_requirements: Construct invalid unvalidated record to disprove automatic invariants
Show validated record rejecting invalid value

items.finding: The v0.20 author note states every nonstatic member class retains its enclosing instance, even without an access. Under the verified Java 21 javac, an unused enclosing-reference field may be elided. Nonstatic construction still requires the enclosing instance, but long-lived memory retention requires actual references.
challenge_requirements: Assert a nonstatic unused-inner constructor has an enclosing-instance parameter
Assert unused-inner class has no outer-reference field in this javac
Assert outer-reading inner retains the synthetic reference
Do not use GC timing as a deterministic validation oracle

items.finding: One-top-level-type-per-file is a design convention, not a language prohibition for multiple package-private top-level types. Duplicate FQNs and mismatched public filenames are separate compile errors.
challenge_requirements: Positive compile multiple distinct package-private classes in one compilation unit
Reject duplicate top-level declarations across files
